problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:{\begin{aligned}x=9-3t \\ y=5+2t \\ z=-7+t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:4x+3y+5z-11=0.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Intersection Between a Line and a Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Intersection Point of a Line in Parametric Form and a Plane in Cartesian Form

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14083348/assets/2989739b62112c05f49beb975eb9039d1bbc7fca39ffd4d0adc058c7cf1cbb41.png)
examples.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+4y+6z+25 & =0 \\ 3(3-4t)+4(-1+2t)+6(2+3t)+25 & =0 \\ 9-12t-4+8t+12+18t+25 & =0 \\ 14t & =-42 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $\mathbf{p}$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-4(-3)=15 \\ y=-1+2(-3)=-7 \\ z=2+3(-3)=-7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(15,-7,-7).$

feedback.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,0,-1⟩+t⟨5,-2,4⟩,\,Π:r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩=22.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's write the equation of the line as

$$
r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩.
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩$ into the equation of the plane, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ ⟨3+5t,-2t,-1+4t⟩\cdot ⟨0,1,-2⟩ & =22 \\ 0(3+5t)+1(-2t)+(-2)(-1+4t) & =22 \\ -2t+2-8t & =22 \\ -10t & =20 \\ t & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$ is obtained by substituting $t=-2$ into the equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨3+5(-2),-2(-2),-1+4(-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-7,4,-9⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intersection point is $P(-7,4,-9).$
